double_advance_guarantee.command: cd backend && uv run pytest tests/unit/test_advance_day.py
double_advance_guarantee.description: NEW check this group, not present in C.json's schema (E6-S2 is the first story to need it): `domain.holdings.service.advance_day` computes `next_date = clock.next_price_date(max(latest NAV price_date))` fresh on every call and relies on the `UNIQUE(asset_class_id, price_date)` DB constraint (not a check-then-act read) to reject a genuine double-advance race, translating the resulting IntegrityError into ConflictError(code=DAY_ALREADY_ADVANCED). EVALUATOR JUDGMENT (see notes for full reasoning): this reasoning was independently verified against system-design.md §9.5 ('the UNIQUE(asset_class_id, price_date) constraint that makes the double-advance edge case a DB-level guarantee rather than a check-then-act race') and D11 ('Double advance-a-day → 409 ... Silent 200 no-op' rejected) and found sound. Two sequential advance_day() calls in the same test process can never naturally collide — the second call legitimately sees the first's committed row and advances to the day after — so the two tests covering this AC (test_advancing_a_second_time_on_the_same_simulated_day_is_rejected, test_advancing_does_not_insert_duplicate_nav_snapshot_rows_after_a_rejected_retry) simulate the losing writer by monkeypatching insert_nav_snapshot to raise the IntegrityError SQLite would raise on the real unique index. This genuinely exercises advance_day's own try/except/rollback/translate-to-ConflictError code path (the part of the production code this AC is actually about) — only the low-level insert call is replaced, not the orchestration logic under test — so it is sound, not merely self-consistent with the mock.

unit_test_checks.assertion: POST /api/auth/login with a valid seeded email/password returns 200 with a body containing access_token (non-empty string) and role matching the seeded user's stored role.
POST /api/auth/login with an incorrect password for an existing email returns 401; the response body contains no access_token key at any level.
POST /api/auth/login with a body missing email, missing password, or with either as an empty string, returns 422 without ever calling domain.auth.service.authenticate.

Neither the 200 login response body nor the 200 GET /api/auth/me response body ever contains a password_hash key or value, confirmed by asserting the key's absence from the parsed JSON, not merely eyeballing the schema.

GET /api/auth/me with no Authorization header, and separately with a malformed Bearer header, both return 401; a valid, unexpired token for any of the four seeded roles is accepted. test_dependencies.py additionally proves require_role(*roles) rejects an authenticated-but-wrong-role caller with 403 ROLE_NOT_PERMITTED and an expired token with 401 TOKEN_EXPIRED.
A valid write_audit_entry(...) call produces exactly one new row in the audit repository, readable back via query_audit_entries with matching id and entity_id.
A call with actor_role in {None, '', 'superadmin', 'customer_service'} (unparametrized set covering missing and out-of-vocabulary values) raises ValidationError and persists no row.
A stand-in downstream risk-band-assignment flow that calls write_audit_entry once, verified via a MagicMock(wraps=...) spy asserting assert_called_once().
Calling write_audit_entry twice for the same entity_id inserts two distinct rows (distinct ids), neither overwriting the other; both remain queryable.
With insert_audit_entry monkeypatched to raise RuntimeError, write_audit_entry propagates that RuntimeError unmodified rather than swallowing it or returning a sentinel.
One call to advance_day() against a freshly seeded database inserts exactly one new NavSnapshot per seeded AssetClass (6), all sharing the same next sequential price_date.

See architecture_checks.double_advance_guarantee for the full reasoning. A simulated losing-writer IntegrityError on the second advance is translated to ConflictError(code=DAY_ALREADY_ADVANCED), and the rollback leaves no duplicate/partial NavSnapshot row behind.
After one advance_day() call, get_latest_nav for a seeded asset class returns the newly inserted snapshot's price_date, not the prior day's.

No scheduler, cron entry, background task, or timer registration exists anywhere in the codebase that calls advance_day; it is reachable only via an explicit function call (confirmed by the absence of any APScheduler/Celery/asyncio.create_task-based periodic trigger in src/app or src/domain, consistent with core/clock.py's own docstring).

A successful advance_day() call recomputes drift for every customer with at least one Holding row (present in result.customers_redrifted) without a separate manual step, confirmed by a customer with seeded holdings, a risk-band assignment, and an active template ending up with a non-empty drift result immediately after advance_day() returns.
compute_drift returns, per held asset class, current_percent, target_percent, and drift_percent == current_percent - target_percent exactly.
No float type appears in any AssetClassDrift field or intermediate value; every value is Decimal or int, confirmed by type() introspection on the dataclass fields.
compute_drift with an empty holdings dict, and separately with holdings summing to zero total value, both return [] without raising (no ZeroDivisionError).
is_over_threshold returns False when abs(drift_bps) == threshold_bps exactly (the exclusive boundary, D13), True when it exceeds by even 1 basis point, and False when below.

For an awkward three-way holding split whose naive per-item rounding would not sum to 10000 bps, the largest-remainder allocation in _allocate_bps_exact still sums current_percent across all held asset classes to exactly 100 (not merely within tolerance).
create_customer_goal with target_amount <= 0 (0 and a negative value) raises ValidationError and persists no row.
create_customer_goal with a target_date strictly before today's date raises ValidationError and persists no row; today's own date is accepted (not rejected as 'past').
Creating a second goal for the same customer_id succeeds and both goals remain independently readable via list_goals_for_customer; the first is neither removed nor overwritten.
update_customer_goal changing only priority is reflected on the next get_goal read and leaves created_at exactly unchanged, while updated_at moves forward.

update_customer_goal called with a customer_id that does not own the target goal_id raises NotFoundError (D12: 404, not 403, so as to not confirm another customer's goal exists) and leaves the goal's fields unchanged.

Already covered by Group B/C's own suites for publish_rule/publish_template/publish_threshold (version = previous_max + 1, prior active row flipped to is_active = false) — re-confirmed passing unmodified this group, no regression.

Inserting a second RiskBandRule/AllocationTemplate/RebalancingThreshold row with a version number matching an already-published row's raises IntegrityError at flush (the DB-level unique index), for all three versioned-publish tables.
None of risk_profile.repository, recommendation.repository, or rebalancing.threshold_repository exposes an update_* callable for its versioned JSON column (getattr-with-default introspection).

update_asset_class edits code and/or name in place and is reflected on the next read; updating to a code already taken by another asset class fails via the existing unique index; renaming/recoding an asset class referenced by a published AllocationTemplate leaves that template's allocations_json (including the referencing asset_class_id and its percent_bps) byte-for-byte unchanged on re-read.
Already covered by Group B/C's own get_active_*/get-by-version suites (a superseded version remains individually queryable by version number, unchanged) — re-confirmed passing unmodified this group.

notes: 1. RESOLVED — layering violation found at initial evaluator sign-off, fixed before commit. architecture_checks.layering scan 2 originally returned one match: backend/src/app/routers/auth.py imported src.domain.auth.repository.get_user_by_id directly for the GET /api/auth/me handler. This was not a carve-out candidate the way Group C's db/session.py/db/engine.py exception was: system-design.md's directory-to-layer table states the API layer 'May NOT import from: domain/*/repository.py (routers never reach past the service layer)', and design decision D3 in the same document names 'Routers may not import repositories' as the chosen design, explicitly rejecting 'Thin pass-through routers reading repos directly' as an alternative — the precise pattern that line implemented. REQUIRED FIX (now applied): domain/auth/service.py now exposes get_user_details(session, user_id), and the router calls that service function instead of importing the repository directly — commit 239cd1e's message documents this fix explicitly ('Fixes a layering violation the evaluator found at sign-off'). Re-verified independently by the evaluator post-fix, against the actual committed source (not the commit message alone): all four layering scans in this check now return zero matches, confirmed by direct read of backend/src/app/routers/auth.py's import list (`from src.domain.auth.service import authenticate, get_user_details`, no repository import anywhere in the file). No test assertions changed as part of the fix.

2. Everything else independently verified clean, both before and re-confirmed after the fix: `uv run pytest -q` (463 passed, 0 failed), `uv run pytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing -q` (100% coverage, 1393/1393 statements, matches the 100% baseline carried from Group C), `uv run ruff check .` (all checks passed), `uv run mypy src/` (0 errors, 52 source files), `uv run pytest tests/architecture/` (52 passed, covering no_float/append_only/allocation_sum together), `uv run detect-secrets scan src seed` (empty results). The other three layering scans (app importing db.models directly, app importing anything from domain/db upward, raise HTTPException anywhere under domain/) returned zero matches from the start.

3. Judgment call E6-S2 AC2 (double-advance rejection via DB-level UNIQUE constraint rather than check-then-act) — VERIFIED SOUND. See architecture_checks.double_advance_guarantee for the full reasoning trail, cross-checked directly against system-design.md §9.5 and D11's text. The monkeypatch-based simulation of the losing writer's IntegrityError is judged a legitimate substitute for true concurrent-session testing (which SQLite/pytest cannot deterministically reproduce), because the code path it proves — advance_day's try/except IntegrityError → session.rollback() → raise ConflictError(DAY_ALREADY_ADVANCED) — is the actual production orchestration logic under test, not a mock of the assertion itself; only the low-level `insert_nav_snapshot` call is replaced.

4. Judgment call E10-S1 scope (AC1/AC3/AC5 pre-satisfied by Group B/C code; only AC4's update_asset_class and AC2's uniqueness tests are new) — VERIFIED, NOT UNDER-SCOPED. Independently re-read publish_rule (risk_profile/repository.py), publish_template (recommendation/repository.py), and publish_threshold (rebalancing/threshold_repository.py): all three already implement version = max(existing) + 1, flip prior is_active to false, and are already covered by Group B/C's own per-module test suites for AC1 and AC5. AC3's 'no mutation of a published row' guarantee is already true structurally (no update_rule/update_template/update_threshold function exists in any of the three modules) and is now explicitly asserted by three new cases in tests/architecture/test_append_only.py rather than merely being true by omission. AC4 (asset-class master CRUD) genuinely had no prior implementation — insert_asset_class existed from E6-S1 but no update path did — and domain/admin/repository.py's update_asset_class is the one new production function this story requires; test_admin_publish_repository.py covers it plus AC2's DB-level uniqueness guarantee for all three versioned-publish tables. This scoping is confirmed correct, not a shortcut.

5. Test-file naming deviates from component-map.md's E2-S2 row, which names `test_auth_login.py`, `test_auth_me.py`, and `test_role_matrix.py` as three separate files. The delivered code consolidates login and /me coverage into `tests/api/test_auth_login.py` and role-matrix coverage into `tests/unit/test_dependencies.py` (built against a throwaway FastAPI app rather than the real router, to test require_role() in isolation from any one endpoint). This is judged an acceptable reorganization, not a coverage gap: every behavior component-map.md attributes to the three named files is present and passing under the two consolidated files, confirmed by direct read of both files' test names against E2-S2's five ACs. Flagged for the lead's awareness only, not a blocking issue — no other story's test file depends on this group's file boundaries the way, e.g., Group C's test_append_only.py ownership did.

6. api_checks are expressed as TestClient-equivalent checks backed 1:1 by tests/api/test_auth_login.py's existing suite rather than a separately-started live uvicorn probe. The task's own instructions treat starting a live server as optional when pytest's api-client tests already exercise the same behavior thoroughly via FastAPI's TestClient, which they do here (real `src.app.main.app` object, real dependency graph, real error handlers) — a live curl pass would exercise identical code paths for no additional signal, so it was not performed.

7. performance_checks is empty this group by design: no new endpoint in this group carries its own NFR-07-style latency requirement distinct from GET /health's, which Group C's contract already covers and which this group does not modify.
